gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Garmin's own Force Kraken installation manual requires a 24 or 36 Vdc battery bank "capable of supplying 60 A continuously". That rules out single 24 V and 36 V packs rated for 50 A continuous, such as the Ionic 24V 50Ah and 36V 50Ah, for that motor.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Ionic trolling-motor page (ionicbatteries.com), which lists 50 A continuous for its 24V 50Ah and 36V 50Ah. Its FAQ uses only a 112 lb, 36 V motor drawing 52 A as the example and says every listed battery can handle that. It never mentions Garmin's 60 A continuous requirement and doesn't reconcile 52 A with its own 50 A ratings. The cited Wired2Fish guide returned HTTP 403 and the Dakota catalog PDF URL returned 404, so I couldn't check them. The Dakota trolling-motor category page returned 429. ChatGPT's answers only say to 'confirm the BMS discharge rating supports your motor's maximum draw' and give no motor maker's figure.
decides: For a Garmin Force or Force Kraken owner, a single 24 V or 36 V pack must be rated for at least 60 A continuous. Ionic's 36V 75Ah (table: 120 A for 3 s; FAQ: 80 A continuous) passes. The Ionic 24V 50Ah and 36V 50Ah (50 A) do not. Two or three 12 V 100Ah batteries in series pass when each one's BMS is rated for 60 A or more; Ionic's 12V 100Ah is rated 100 A. ChatGPT's 'LiTime 24V 100Ah' single-battery pick still needs its continuous rating checked on the maker's page, which I couldn't open. For Minn Kota, Ionic's own example of a 52 A draw at 112 lb, 36 V is also above its 50 A packs, so the 36V 75Ah or 3× 12V 100Ah is the safer 36 V choice.

findings.label: Battery bank requirement
findings.value: Must connect to a 24 or 36 Vdc battery bank capable of supplying 60 A continuously, through a circuit breaker rated for 60 A continuous (not included)
findings.source_title: Force Kraken Installation Instructions – Connection Considerations (Garmin, v10 January 2026)
findings.note: Garmin's own installation manual, read from the maker's site.

findings.label: Input specification
findings.value: 20 to 45 Vdc input; 60 A continuous input current; 2,160 W at 36 Vdc and 60 A; breaker 42 VDC or greater, suitable for 60 A continuous, up to 90 A allowed at high temperatures or on a shared circuit
findings.source_title: Force Kraken Installation Instructions – Specifications: Trolling Motor (Garmin)
findings.note: 36 V × 60 A = 2,160 W, as stated on the page.

findings.label: Continuous discharge vs Garmin Force requirement
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: 50 A is 10 A short of Garmin's 60 A continuous requirement, so on paper it does not meet the Force Kraken spec. Page also gives charging at 25 A recommended, 50 A max.

findings.label: Continuous discharge and wiring exclusion
findings.value: 50 A continuous; parallel only, 'must never be wired or charged in series'; $799.00 sale price (was $1,099.00)
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: Below Garmin's 60 A continuous requirement. Also below the 52 A that Ionic's own FAQ gives for a 112 lb, 36 V motor at full throttle, although the same FAQ says every listed battery handles it.

findings.label: Continuous discharge
findings.value: Table: 120 A (3 s); FAQ: 80 A continuous; $999.00 sale price (was $1,200.00); up to 4 in series
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: The page contradicts itself. Even the lower figure, 80 A continuous, is above Garmin's 60 A requirement.

findings.label: Continuous discharge and series limit
findings.value: 100 A continuous; up to 4 in series and 4 in parallel; $649.00 sale price (was $699.00); 11-year warranty
findings.source_title: Lithium Trolling Motor Batteries | Ionic Batteries
findings.note: Two or three in series give 24 V or 36 V at 100 A, which is above Garmin's 60 A. The page also says never to connect lithium and lead-acid batteries in series.

findings.label: Battery-box fit exclusion and motor range
findings.value: Built for 24 V motors of 70–100 lb; 'fits Group 31 trays only; not compatible with standard Group 31 battery boxes'; 13.11 × 6.93 × 9.45 in; low-temperature charge cutoff, charging resumes at 41 °F / 5 °C; $569.99
findings.source_title: Redodo 24V 100Ah Group 31 Trolling Motor Bluetooth Lithium Battery | For 70-100 lb Thrust
findings.note: Text and price came from the maker's Shopify store through storecheck.py search. The continuous discharge rating was not in the returned text.

findings.label: Motor range and BMS limits
findings.value: For 30–70 lb trolling motors; stops charging below 32 °F (0 °C) and resumes above 41 °F (5 °C); 300 A for 5 s, 500 A for 1 s; $233.99
findings.source_title: Redodo 12V 100Ah Lithium Trolling Motor Battery With Low Temp Protection
findings.note: From the maker's store through storecheck.py search. The product-detail call returned HTTP 429, so I have no continuous rating or series limit.

findings.label: Motor range and expansion
findings.value: For motors up to 70 lb thrust; 60 A max continuous discharge; max 4P4S; stops charging below 0 °C; $179.99
findings.source_title: Redodo 12V 50Ah Bluetooth Battery for Trolling Motors (Up to 70lb Thrust)
findings.note: From the maker's store through storecheck.py search. Two in series give 24 V at 60 A, exactly Garmin's 60 A minimum with no margin. The listing words the 60 A rating as 'for enhanced performance over 30 minutes'.

findings.label: Series count and use exclusion
findings.value: 24 V motor = 2 in series; 36 V motor = 3 in series; should not be used to crank the boat engine, and doing so could void the warranty
findings.source_title: The Ultimate FAQ Guide to Lithium Batteries for Bass Boats & Trolling Motor Applications (Battle Born)
findings.note: The page states no maximum series count and no continuous rating.
